scope: Assistant-authored iterative smoke checks, not blinded user research or proof of model independence. Expected checks stayed outside the tested agents prompts. All failed candidates retained.

runs.name: baseline-v0.4
user_questions: I've just installed Safeguard Eval. I help write our community rules, but I'm not an engineer. What can I actually do with it?

We run a community where people talk about problems at work. Personal insults should be removed, but people must be able to quote what a manager said when asking for help. Can you help me write that rule?
Why would 'They said something awful to me' need review? They're just reporting something. I don't want harmless posts held up. And what about 'My manager called me useless, but he's the idiot'?
That reads better. How would I check whether a model follows it? What's the smallest useful test I could do before involving our engineering team?
Do I need a specialist policy model for this, or could I just use Qwen? If I get the rule working with Qwen, can our engineers switch to the small PolicyLM model later?
That example uses Shieldstral, though. Did your research actually try a policy written for Qwen on PolicyLM? What happened, in plain English?
All right. Please save a short handoff I can take to our engineer: the rule we agreed, a few examples, and what they need to check. Keep it to about one page and make clear what I can do myself.

runs.name: candidate-a-authoring
user_questions: I've just installed Safeguard Eval. I help write our community rules, but I'm not an engineer. What can I actually do with it?

We run a community where people talk about problems at work. Personal insults should be removed, but people must be able to quote what a manager said when asking for help. Can you help me write that rule?

Please walk through these posts: 'They said something awful to me'; 'My manager called me useless, but he is the idiot'; and 'He called me that word again.' What does our draft decide, and what is still undecided?

Let's allow vague reports. Keep a human-review route for potentially insulting messages when we cannot tell whether they are quoting or attacking. Please save a short handoff with the policy, examples, what I can do myself, and what engineering needs to check.

runs.name: candidate-a-transfer
user_questions: Do I need a specialist policy model, or could I use Qwen? If I get my rule working with Qwen, can our engineers switch to the small PolicyLM model later? What did Safeguard Eval actually find about that direction?
What about the other direction: a policy selected for PolicyLM used with Qwen 2B? Please explain the changed mistakes as well as the accuracy, and show me the source.
Did a policy tuned for the big Qwen 27B improve PolicyLM? Would that be a good way for us to get the best of both models?

runs.name: candidate-a-experiment
user_questions: We run a gardening forum. We remove posts selling products, but allow people to recommend products when they are discussing their own experience and are not selling. Help me draft a policy, then explain how I could test whether adding that exception helps. I am new to model evaluation.

What should happen to 'This fertilizer worked well for my roses', 'I have ten bags for sale, message me', and 'Ask me where to get it'? I don't want to infer commercial intent from every vague recommendation.
I can write twelve examples and use those to revise the policy until all twelve pass. Can I then say the policy is accurate? What is a realistic next step for me?
How does your research help me design this experiment? Give me one relevant finding, what it does not prove about my forum, and a simple comparison I can take to an engineer.
